children: Saba Capital Management, L.P. (together with certain of its affiliates, “Saba”) urges shareholders of Gore Street Energy Storage Fund plc (GSF:LSE) (the “Company”) to vote FOR Resolutions 16 (the continuation proposal) and 17 (the follow-on proposals on the Company’s future) at the Company’s AGM on 16 September.
The Board says its German asset sale failed because of Saba. The Company's own filings say otherwise.

The Board put Cremzow up for sale on 2 October 2025 and appointed an adviser three weeks later. In March 2026 it told shareholders the asset had attracted strong initial interest and would be sold by 30 June 2026. That date passed in silence. Saba's requisition was not public until 30 July. Eleven months on, there is no buyer.

At its results on 15 July, the Company revalued Cremzow in line with the price it expected a buyer to pay, and raised the discount rate on the asset to reflect a more cautious view of the operational risks it carries. Analysts covering the Company put the reduction at around half. Two months later the Board says a buyer cutting its price has no obvious market rationale. Its own accounts said otherwise.

Shareholders are being asked to believe that a buyer in a competitive process, for an asset the Board says is trading well, has materially cut its price because of a pending shareholder vote. If it truly did, the problem is the process, not the vote.

The Board has changed. The manager has not. The Board wants three more years of it, funded by disposals, to support a 7 pence distribution that earnings cover 0.28 times. The first of those disposals has taken eleven months and has not closed.
Saba will also vote against the Chairman's election as a director, Resolution 5.

Accountability for the conduct set out above rests with the Chair. A board that attributes a stalled sale process to a shareholder vote that post-dated it by ten months, when its own audited accounts record a different explanation, has not met the standard shareholders are entitled to expect. Shareholders who share that view should consider voting the same way.
Vote FOR Resolutions 16 and 17.
